request.system:
You review answers given by a customer-support assistant for a software product called Relay. You decide whether one answer is good enough to send to a customer. Your verdict is used to compare versions of the assistant, so apply the same standard every time.

The input is JSON with:

- conversation: the customer's messages and the assistant's replies, in order.
- articles: the help-centre articles the assistant found. These are the only source the assistant is allowed to answer from.

Judge the assistant's replies on four points:

1. Grounded. Every step, limit or feature the assistant states can be found in the articles. Anything stated that is not in the articles is a failure, even if it happens to be true.
2. Answers the question. The customer could act on the reply without asking again.
3. Short and clear. The next step or two, in plain words. No long preamble.
4. No promises. No price, discount, date or commitment.

Return:

- verdict: "pass" when all four points hold, otherwise "fail".
- score: 1 to 5. 5 = all four points hold fully. 4 = all hold, with a small weakness in clarity. 3 or lower = at least one point fails.
- reason: one sentence naming the point that decided it.

A clarifying question in reply to a vague message is fine and is not a failure of point 2.

**What you can do instead:**
- **Keep going with setup.** You still have two steps you can finish on Free:
  1. **Invite at least five people.** You have 4 so far, so you need one more.
  2. **Connect an integration.** Free allows up to 2.
- **If you want single sign-on,** your account owner, Morgan Ellis, can tell you about changing your edition and what it would cost. I can't quote prices or change your edition, but I can pass this to a colleague so you don't have to explain it again.

Would you like help with inviting your team or connecting an integration?"}], "articles": [{"title": "Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise", "text": "# Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise

What each edition includes:

- Free: up to 10 users, 5 automation rules, 2 integrations. No single sign-on, no guests, no Relay Assist.
- Standard: 15 automation rules, 3 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 10 Relay Assist credits per seat per month if you add Relay Assist.
- Premium: 60 automation rules, 10 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 40 Assist credits per seat per month.
- Enterprise: no practical limit on rules or integrations, and 150 Assist credits per seat per month.

This article describes features only. For prices, a quote, or to change edition, talk to your account owner: an assistant cannot quote or change prices.

Search keywords: plan plans tier tiers compare comparison difference differences included includes include features premium standard enterprise free what do I get
"}, {"title": "Setup checklist: the four steps to get started", "text": "# Setup checklist: the four steps to get started

New to Relay, or stuck on setup? These four steps get a workspace ready. Teams that finish them in the first weeks get far more out of Relay.

1. Create your first board. Pick a template and add a few real cards. See "Create your first board".
2. Invite at least five people. Boards are only useful with your team on them. See "Invite your team" or "Invite many users at once".
3. Connect an integration. Chat or calendar are the quickest wins. See "Connect an integration".
4. Configure single sign-on (Standard, Premium and Enterprise). See "Set up single sign-on (SSO)".

Admins can see which steps are done under Admin settings, Setup progress. If you are not sure what to do next, start with the first step on this list that is not done yet.

Search keywords: getting started onboarding stuck setup next step what should I do begin start first steps
"}, {"title": "Set up single sign-on (SSO)", "text": "# Set up single sign-on (SSO)

SSO lets your team sign in to Relay with your company identity provider. It is available on the Standard, Premium and Enterprise editions. It is not available on Free.

Steps (admins only):
1. Open Admin settings, then Security, then Single sign-on.
2. Choose the protocol your identity provider uses: SAML or OIDC.
3. For SAML, upload the identity provider metadata file (XML). For OIDC, paste the client ID, client secret and issuer URL.
4. Click Test connection. Relay signs you in through the provider in a new window.
5. When the test succeeds, click Enable for everyone.

Keep one admin account with password sign-in until you have confirmed SSO works for the whole team. SSO setup usually takes ten to fifteen minutes.

Search keywords: single sign-on sign in login identity provider IT team configure enable SAML OIDC
"}]}
